thread:
june: Hey team — our customers are seeing a bunch of 429s from the /v1/rerank endpoint since yesterday afternoon. Happened right after a small feature flag rollout. Responses look like {"error": "rate_limited"} and scores are missing for some items. Any quick checks?
maya: Sorry you're hitting this, june. Can you paste a raw request (headers + body) and a sample 429 response? Is this from a single region or multiple?
june: here you go (sanitized):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"query":"best pizza toppings","candidates":["pepperoni","mushroom","pineapple",...],"project":"june-co"}'

Response (429):
{"error":"rate_limited","message":"quota exceeded for rerank.qps"}
Headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 30, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 6

Traffic looks steady ~10 QPS normally. This spike was only +5 QPS for a ~10s window after rollout.
liam: Thanks. Two things to check quickly: 1) are you sending one candidate-per-request (many tiny calls) vs batching many candidates? Rerank has a separate QPS pool and per-candidate cost. 2) See if the requests are being routed to multiple model variants (could double-charge quota if fallback routing duplicates calls).

Can you run a quick request log grep on your side for 1xx/2xx vs 429 counts by route?
maya: Also note we recently rolled a per-project rerank quota change (backend config) that accidentally introduced a lower default for new projects. june-co might still be on the old default. I'll check our quota service.
june: Grep shows ~85% 200, 15% 429 during the 30s window. Most 429s have Retry-After 6 or 10. We batch ~8 candidates per call (that's our normal pattern).
liam: Good to know. Batching 8 should be fine generally. The 429s with Retry-After suggest hitting the per-project QPS cap not the global one. Two immediate mitigations: 1) add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s, 2) temporarily reduce client QPS (throttle) or increase batch size to reduce QPS. Batching more reduces requests per second but increases per-request work (watch token limits).
oscar: Jumping in from platform — I'm seeing that june-co is on rerank.qps = 30 by default. The rollout triggered an extra health-checking worker that caused a burst of duplicated rerank attempts for a short window. That pushed them above 30 qps and exhausted the token bucket. There's also a known rollover bug where bursting near bucket refill can prematurely cap remaining tokens; we're rolling a fix.

Temporary plan: I'll bump june-co to 80 rerank.qps for 24h and keep an eye. If you need longer term, we can set a reserved capacity or adjust autoscale thresholds.

deploy-bot: patch: platform/quotas  -> increase-defaults for rerank; cid: deploy-98765 

maya: Oscar — can you confirm the scope of the fix? Is it server-side token-bucket only, or do we need a client-safe header change? Also, customers should be able to see X-RateLimit headers, right?
oscar: Fix is server-side in the quota allocator; will prevent the premature cap when refill aligns with burst. We will also add more granular headers in the next sprint to show per-route window and long-term quota. For now X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining are accurate.

I bumped june-co to 80 qps; you'll see the change within 60s.
liam: For SRE, I'll add a short-term alert rule: if >5% requests to /v1/rerank return 429 for >60s, page on-call. Also adding a dashboard tile showing per-project rerank qps vs limit so support can triage faster.
maya: june — while we monitor, please implement backoff and if possible increase per-request batch size to 20 candidates (watch token limit) to reduce calls. Also set a client-side circuit that pauses rerank calls for 5s after 3 consecutive 429s.
june: Will do the backoff + batch increase. Curious — any guidance on optimal batch size? We sometimes see scoring slightly off when we include too many candidates (we thought it might be truncation).
liam: Rerank scoring itself shouldn't be nondeterministic due to batch size, but if you hit token truncation or model-level input limits (like max context tokens) that can cause partial inputs and weird scores. Keep per-request token usage < 4096 for the model you're pinned to. If you need >4096 consider chunking and reranking in stages.
maya: I'm going to mark this thread for follow-up and assign a ticket to platform to patch the rollover bug and add audit logs for quota adjustments. Oscar — can you paste the internal ticket ID once created?
oscar: created: PLT-4321 — quota allocator rollover bug + telemetry. ETA for rollout of fix: 48h. I'll also request a small UI flag to let support bump rerank.qps for 24h without escalations.
maya: Perfect. june — after you add backoff and batch bump, let us know if 429s stop. If they persist, we'll extend the temp quota increase. :thumbsup:
june: Thanks everyone — applying client changes now. Will report back in ~10m. :pray:
